- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. I have a complete picture now. Here is the full report.

## Summary

A **one-way, manual, push-only** Todoist sync already exists (app → Todoist), added in commit `e27fcde` ("Add push sync to Todoist for tasks and e-blasts", Aug 21 2026) and tweaked in `c25ea84` ("Default synced Todoist tasks to 9:00 AM instead of 11:59 PM", Sep 2 2026). It explicitly mirrors the existing Google Calendar sync architecture. There is **no pull/inbound direction, no webhook, no polling, and no cron job** — sync only happens when a user clicks a "Push to Todoist" button.

### 1. Files referencing "todoist"

Backend (`artifacts/api-server/src/`):
- `lib/todoist-client.ts` — Todoist API wrapper
- `routes/todoist.ts` — sync route logic (mounted at `/export/todoist`)
- `routes/index.ts:14,30` — `router.use("/export/todoist", todoistRouter)`
- `routes/shows.ts:2,226-227,241-249` — on show delete, orphans Todoist task IDs
- `routes/tasks.ts:2,140,147-148` — on task delete, orphans its Todoist task ID
- `routes/eblasts.ts:2,139,146-147` — on e-blast delete, orphans its Todoist task ID

Frontend (`artifacts/show-command-center/src/`):
- `contexts/todoist-context.tsx` — React context storing chosen Todoist project IDs (localStorage key `todoist_prefs`) and fetching project list
- `components/todoist-settings.tsx` — Settings-page UI to pick a Todoist project per item type
- `pages/settings.tsx:38,369` — renders `<TodoistSettings />`
- `pages/show-detail.tsx:4,6,47-74,268-271` — "Push to Todoist" button on a show's detail page
- `pages/calendar.tsx:4,6,43-70,260-265` — "Push to Todoist" button on the calendar page
- `App.tsx:7,36,43` — wraps app in `<TodoistProvider>`

DB schema (`lib/db/`):
- `src/schema/tasks.ts:16` — `todoistTaskId: text("todoist_task_id")`
- `src/schema/eblasts.ts:15` — `todoistTaskId: text("todoist_task_id")`
- `src/schema/todoistOrphans.ts` — dedicated `todoist_orphans` table
- `src/schema/index.ts:9` — exports the orphans table
- `migrations/0007_material_betty_ross.sql` + `migrations/meta/0007_snapshot.json` — migration adding the above

Generated API layer (auto-generated from OpenAPI, not hand-written):
- `lib/api-spec/openapi.yaml:768-833,1468-1489` — `/export/todoist/projects` (GET), `/export/todoist/sync` (POST), `TodoistProject` / `TodoistSyncResult` schemas
- `lib/api-zod/src/generated/...` and `lib/api-client-react/src/generated/...` — generated types/hooks (`useListTodoistProjects`, `useSyncTodoist`)

### 2. How the sync mechanism works

**One-way only: app → Todoist.** Nothing pulls changes back from Todoist into the app's DB (no reverse mapping of "if closed in Todoist, mark completed here").

**Trigger:** Manual only — a "Push to Todoist" button on the Show Detail page (`show-detail.tsx:268-271`) and the Calendar page (`calendar.tsx:260-265`). No cron, no webhook, no polling exists anywhere in the repo (confirmed via grep across `.ts` files for `cron`/`webhook`/`schedule`).

**Endpoint:** `POST /export/todoist/sync` (`artifacts/api-server/src/routes/todoist.ts`, function starting at `router.post("/sync", ...)`), optionally scoped by `showId` query param, plus `taskProjectId`/`eblastProjectId` to pick target Todoist projects.

**Logic per sync run:**
1. Loads all shows (or one), then all tasks/e-blasts for those shows.
2. For each task/e-blast with no `dueDate`: if it has a stored `todoistTaskId`, deletes the Todoist task and clears the column (handles "unset due date" case).
3. Otherwise builds a Todoist task body via `makeTodoistTask()` (content = `"{name} [{showName}]"`, description includes show/category/notes, `due_string` = `"{dueDate} 09:00"` with `due_lang: "en"`).
4. If `todoistTaskId` already stored: `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}` to update it (404 → treated as deleted upstream, falls through to recreate).
5. If none: `POST /api/v1/tasks` to create, stores the returned Todoist ID back into `tasksTable.todoistTaskId` / `eblastsTable.todoistTaskId`.
6. Completion state is pushed via native open/closed state: `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/close` or `/reopen` based on the local `completed`/`sent` boolean — not a text-prefix hack (this was an explicit design choice per the commit message, contrasted with the older Google Calendar approach).
7. Runs with concurrency batches of 5 (`CONCURRENCY = 5`).
8. After main sync, `drainOrphans()` processes the `todoist_orphans` table (populated when a task/eblast/show is deleted locally) and deletes those Todoist tasks too, then removes the orphan rows.
9. Response returns `{ ok, created, updated, deleted }` counters.

**Auth to Todoist:** Uses Replit's managed OAuth connector, not a raw API key. `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/todoist-client.ts` instantiates `new ReplitConnectors()` (from `@replit/connectors-sdk`) and calls `connectors.proxy("todoist", path, {...})`. This is the same pattern used for Google Calendar (`lib/google-calendar-client.ts`). It includes 429 rate-limit retry with exponential backoff (`MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES = 5`, `RATE_LIMIT_BASE_DELAY_MS = 500`).

There is also `GET /export/todoist/projects` (`todoistListProjects()`) to list the user's Todoist projects for the picker UI.

### 3. DB schema fields for external IDs / sync state

- `tasksTable.todoistTaskId` (`text`, nullable) — `lib/db/src/schema/tasks.ts:16`
- `eblastsTable.todoistTaskId` (`text`, nullable) — `lib/db/src/schema/eblasts.ts:15`
- `todoistOrphansTable` (`lib/db/src/schema/todoistOrphans.ts`): `id`, `todoistTaskId` (not null), `itemType` (default `"task"`, also used for `"eblast"`), `createdAt`
- No sync-timestamp column exists (no `lastSyncedAt`/`syncedAt` field anywhere), no sync-status enum, and no Todoist project ID stored per-task (project choice is only a global-ish per-type localStorage preference on the frontend, not persisted per-task/show in the DB).
- Analogous but separate Google Calendar columns exist for comparison: `gcalEventId` on both tables, and a `gcal_orphans` table (`lib/db/src/schema/gcalOrphans.ts`) with `calendarType` field — same orphan-cleanup pattern reused for Todoist.

### 4. API keys / env vars

No Todoist API key or env var exists anywhere (`.env`, `.env.example`, README, config). Checked `artifacts/show-command-center/.env` — only contains `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`. Auth is entirely delegated to the Replit Connectors SDK (`connectors.proxy("todoist", ...)`), which manages OAuth tokens outside this repo's codebase/env files.

### 5. UI elements

- **Settings page** (`pages/settings.tsx`): `<TodoistSettings />` block with two `<Select>` project pickers ("Tasks →" and "e-Blasts →" project assignment), backed by `todoist-context.tsx`/`todoist-settings.tsx`.
- **Show Detail page** (`pages/show-detail.tsx:268-271`): outline button "Push to Todoist" (icon `ListTodo`, spinner while `syncTodoist.isPending`), triggers `handleTodoistSync` which calls `useSyncTodoist()` scoped to that show; shows a toast with created/updated/deleted counts on success/failure.
- **Calendar page** (`pages/calendar.tsx:260-265`): identical "Push to Todoist" button, but unscoped (or scoped to `selectedShowId` if one is chosen in the calendar filter).
- No badges, no per-task "synced" indicator, no Todoist-status icon in task lists — just the two push buttons and the settings project pickers.

### 6. Git log


`e27fcde` full message: "Mirrors the existing Google Calendar sync architecture (client wrapper, sync route with create/update/orphan-cleanup, per-item-type project picker) but maps completion to Todoist's native open/closed task state via close/reopen calls instead of a text-prefix hack. Adds todoist_task_id tracking columns and a todoist_orphans table so deleted tasks/e-blasts get their Todoist task removed on next sync." — touched 30 files, 1572 insertions.

### Implications for planning a full two-way sync

Since the existing system is push-only with no webhook/polling and no `lastSyncedAt`/sync-status tracking, a two-way sync would need to add: an inbound mechanism (Todoist webhooks require a public HTTPS endpoint + webhook secret verification, or polling via `find-completed-tasks`/activity log), conflict-resolution logic (e.g. last-write-wins using a timestamp field that doesn't currently exist), and likely a new `todoist.ts` route or additional endpoints for receiving/pulling updates, plus new DB columns (e.g. `todoistSyncedAt`, `todoistUpdatedAt` or a sync-status enum) since none currently exist beyond the raw `todoistTaskId` pointer.
